## Empirical signal (2026-05-04)

CAPTAIN_ARGUS for ariadne--xft.4 cited git blame to claim 'docstring authored by PRINCIPAL himself in commit ebb9ecca (2026-04-21)' as a load-bearing argument against option A. PRINCIPAL: 'I am 100% sure I did not personally write that.' Verified: commit ebb9ecca is git-literally-attributed to denson (his git config), but it's a ticket-driven gauntlet commit ('Add OAuth middleware tests (ariadne--xft.2)') — almost certainly written by some Ada/CAPTAIN session committing AS PRINCIPAL's git identity per standard workspace practice.

PRINCIPAL flagged: 'Can't we just have the agents tag git authorship to indicate the exact agent that really did it?'

Yes. Direct, structural fix instead of defensive 'warn agents not to infer.'

## The proposal

Agents commit with their own configured git identity, not PRINCIPAL's. git blame then shows the actual seat that wrote each line. Zero inference needed at read time — the data IS the identity.

Format proposal:
- Author name: '<MNEMONIC>_<slug>' or '<MNEMONIC>' (user-tier no slug)
- Author email: '<mnemonic-slug>@<project>.local' or similar non-routing local-only domain
- Examples:
  - 'CAPTAIN_ADA_ariadne_core <captain-ada@ariadne-core.local>'
  - 'MAJOR_PLINY_the_stoa <major-pliny@the-stoa.local>'
  - 'MAJOR_POLYBIUS <polybius@user-tier.local>'
  - 'CAPTAIN_DAEDALUS_ariadne_core <captain-daedalus@ariadne-core.local>'

PRINCIPAL keeps using 'denson <densonsmith2@gmail.com>' for hand-authored commits. Now distinguishable from agent commits by author field.

## Implementation options

### Option A: per-commit override via git -c flags

Agents use 'git -c user.name="<seat>" -c user.email="<seat>@local" commit -m "..."' for each commit. Override is per-command, no config persistence.

Pro: zero config-state to manage; works in any worktree without setup.
Con: easy to forget; agents must remember to override every commit.

### Option B: worktree-local git config

When MAJOR_PLINY (or any orchestrator) creates a worktree for a CAPTAIN to work in, also runs 'git -C <worktree> config user.name <seat>' and 'git -C <worktree> config user.email <seat>@local'. CAPTAIN commits inside the worktree pick up the local config automatically.

Pro: agents don't need to override per-commit; worktree-local config handles it.
Pro: composes with existing worktree-per-ticket discipline.
Con: requires setup at worktree-create time; PLINY brief must include the git-config step.
Con: doesn't help commits made outside worktrees (e.g., POLYBIUS substrate edits on main).

### Option C: agent role file specifies identity + mandatory pre-commit

Each CAPTAIN / MAJOR role file declares the agent's seat-identity. Role file contains explicit instruction: 'Before any git commit, set user.name + user.email via git config (or -c override). Format: <mnemonic>_<slug>.'

Pro: discipline is in the role file; agents remember because the role tells them.
Pro: works in any context (worktree or not).
Con: relies on agents reading + following; no enforcement.

### Option D: hybrid — B for worktrees, C for non-worktree commits

PLINY sets worktree-local config when creating worktrees (B). Role files instruct agents to verify identity before committing (C, fallback when no worktree-local config).

My lean: D. Worktree-local handles the common case automatically; role-file discipline catches the edge cases.

## Where in substrate

1. **install.sh** — at install time, write a small helper script (substrate/scripts/git-identity.sh or similar) that any agent can call to set identity. Or: install.sh itself doesn't write git config; that's per-engagement.

2. **MAJOR_PLINY role file** — gauntlet dispatch instructions add a 'git config when creating worktree' step. PLINY brief to CAPTAINs includes the identity to use.

3. **All CAPTAIN role files** — pre-commit identity discipline (verify user.name/email is the seat, not PRINCIPAL).

4. **MAJOR_POLYBIUS role file** — substrate-edit commits also use POLYBIUS identity, not PRINCIPAL.

5. **operating-disciplines.md** — universal team protocol section on commit-author identity.

6. **Substrate templates** — paste-instruction template + activation paste cheatsheet may need git-identity setup notes.

## Trade-offs against current state

Pro: git blame becomes accurate at line level. ARGUS-style 'PRINCIPAL wrote this' inferences become correct (or correctly identify the agent).
Pro: PR reviews can distinguish agent contributions from human-PRINCIPAL contributions.
Pro: enables future analytics ('which seat writes the most code').

Con: PR contributor lists become more cluttered (agents become listed contributors).
Con: GitHub Co-Authored-By trailer existing convention may need adjustment (or supersession by primary-author identity).
Con: For PUBLIC repos like ariadne-core, listed agent authors may confuse external viewers (mitigation: use clear naming + maybe a public note in CONTRIBUTING.md explaining the convention).

## Sequencing

This is a substantive substrate addition. Could fold into arc-21 (currently being revised) or file as arc-22 follow-up. POLYBIUS_the_stoa's call. Strong case for arc-22 since arc-21 is already 11 tickets and this is a separate concern (commit-author convention vs coordination protocol).

## Reference

- ariadne--xft.4 ARGUS git-blame inference incident (2026-05-04) — empirical anchor
- Global ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md authorship-attribution rule — same family of concern (don't conflate human authorship with git-attributed authorship)
- stoa--e39 (bw-timeline parsing) — sibling discipline (data-tagging at write time prevents inference at read time)
- stoa--m5m (positive references only) — sibling discipline (substrate teaches agents to communicate clearly)

title: Per-agent git identity for commits — agents commit with their own configured git author so blame indicates the actual seat
